config.title: Grid: container and template

intro.title: Grid: container and template
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout using CSS Grid to arrange content into rows and columns. You will learn the core concept of defining a grid container and specifying its template structure. The main technologies involved are CSS Grid properties like `display: grid`, `grid-template-columns`, and `grid-template-rows`. This beginner-friendly lesson will guide you through creating a structured layout step by step, helping you understand how to control the placement of elements on a page.
intro.usecase: CSS Grid's container and template properties are foundational for building complex, responsive layouts in modern web applications. Developers use them to create structured interfaces like product dashboards with aligned data panels, media galleries with consistent image grids, and content-heavy pages with sidebars and main areas. Mastering these concepts allows you to efficiently arrange UI components—such as filter controls, data cards, or navigation menus—into predictable, maintainable layouts that adapt seamlessly across devices.

objectives: Initialize a CSS Grid container by applying the display: grid property
Configure grid template columns using fixed, flexible, and fractional units
Construct grid template rows to define the vertical structure of your layout
Implement grid template areas to create named layout regions
Manipulate grid gap properties to control spacing between rows and columns
Apply grid auto-flow to control how auto-placed items fill the grid
Integrate grid template shorthand to efficiently define the complete grid structure

steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up basic HTML structure
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and prepare HTML with a container element and child elements to style with Grid. Start by creating a CSS file named 'styles.css' and adding a basic HTML structure with a container div and several child divs inside it.
steps.hint: You'll need to create a CSS file and write HTML with a container div that will become your grid container, plus several child divs that will be your grid items.

steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a CSS file and HTML with a container element containing several child elements, ready to be styled with CSS Grid.
successCriteria: A CSS file is created with a container div and multiple child divs inside it, forming the basic structure for grid practice.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both a container element and several child elements inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a CSS file and HTML structure with a container div and multiple child divs inside it.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the container element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a container element with a width of 800px, height of 400px, and a light blue background color (#e6f7ff).
steps.hint: Use a class selector like .container and set the width, height, and background-color properties.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create your CSS file and HTML structure here */

/* Add your container styling below */
steps.expectedOutcome: A visible container element with defined dimensions and background color.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a rule for a container element with width: 800px, height: 400px, and background-color: #e6f7ff.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but check that you have all three properties: width, height, and background-color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container styling is missing or incomplete. Add width, height, and background-color to make the container visible.

steps.title: Style the child elements inside the container
steps.instruction: Add padding, background colors, and borders to the child elements to make them visually distinct as grid items.
steps.hint: Use CSS properties like padding, background-color, and border on the child elements to create clear visual separation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The child elements will have padding, background colors, and borders applied to distinguish them as individual grid items.
successCriteria: Child elements have padding, background-color, and border properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include all three: padding, background-color, and border properties for the child elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child elements don't have the required styling. Add padding, background-color, and border properties to make them visually distinct.

steps.title: Declare the container as a Grid container
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property 'display: grid' to your container element's styling to activate CSS Grid layout.
steps.hint: Look for the container selector in your CSS and add 'display: grid;' inside its rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container element will be transformed into a CSS Grid container, enabling grid layout properties for its children.
successCriteria: The container selector includes the property 'display: grid'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added 'display: grid' to the container selector. Check that the property is spelled correctly and ends with a semicolon.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container isn't yet a Grid container. Look for the '.container' selector in your CSS and add 'display: grid;' inside it to activate CSS Grid layout.

steps.title: Define the grid template columns
steps.instruction: Inside the .container rule, add the grid-template-columns property to create three equal-width columns.
steps.hint: Use grid-template-columns with a value that repeats three equal fractions of the available space.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule will include grid-template-columns to define three equal columns.
successCriteria: The .container rule contains grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); or equivalent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using grid-template-columns to create exactly three equal columns.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added grid-template-columns inside the .container rule with a value that creates three equal columns.

steps.title: Define the grid template rows
steps.instruction: Add a grid-template-rows property to the .container rule to create two rows with specific heights. Make the first row 100px tall and the second row 200px tall.
steps.hint: Use the grid-template-rows property with two values separated by a space, like: grid-template-rows: 100px 200px;
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule should include a grid-template-rows property with two height values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added grid-template-rows with exactly two height values (100px and 200px) to the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-rows property is missing or incorrect. Add grid-template-rows: 100px 200px; to the .container rule.

steps.title: Add gap between grid items
steps.instruction: Add the 'gap' property to the .container rule to create spacing between grid items.
steps.hint: The 'gap' property sets the spacing between rows and columns. You can use a single value like '20px' for equal spacing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid items will have consistent spacing between them when you preview the layout.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes a 'gap' property with a valid value (e.g., '20px').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added the 'gap' property to the .container rule with a value like '20px'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gap property is missing or incorrect. Add 'gap: 20px;' (or similar) to the .container rule.

steps.title: Experiment with different column values
steps.instruction: In the .container rule, modify the grid-template-columns property to use a combination of different units: percentages, pixels, and fr units.
steps.hint: Try using values like 30%, 200px, and 1fr to create a flexible layout with mixed sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have columns sized with mixed units, demonstrating flexible and fixed column sizing.
successCriteria: The grid-template-columns property in .container uses at least two different unit types (e.g., percentage, pixel, fr).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using at least two different unit types in grid-template-columns.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've modified the grid-template-columns property in the .container rule with mixed units.

steps.title: Experiment with different row values
steps.instruction: In the .container selector, modify the grid-template-rows property to use a combination of auto, minmax(), and fixed height units like 100px.
steps.hint: Try values like 'auto 100px minmax(50px, 200px)' to create rows with different sizing behaviors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have rows with different sizing behaviors: one auto-sized, one fixed at 100px, and one flexible between 50px and 200px.
successCriteria: The .container selector includes a grid-template-rows property with at least three values using auto, a fixed unit (like 100px), and minmax().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your grid-template-rows includes at least three values using auto, a fixed unit (like 100px), and minmax().
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-rows property needs to be modified with specific values. Try using 'auto 100px minmax(50px, 200px)' or similar combinations.
